As expected, mixing has a very strong influence upon the rate of the phase transfer reaction, which proceeds faster at higher agitation speeds. If adequate dispersion of the aqueous and organic phases is not achieved, as was the case at 200 rpm in this series of experiments, the reaction may not be complete even after 24 hours. Even though only 70% conversion was reached after 24 hours at 200 rpm, reaction completion was achieved in 1.5 hours after increasing the agitation rate to disperse the phases.

Despite these results, the reaction appears robust enough such that in all of the experiments, product purity profiles were typical for all of the complete reactions, and issues with purity related to mixing are not anticipated upon scale-up.

Continued stressing experiments were executed to understand if there is any impact on prolonged time difference between laboratory and manufacturing times on the quality attributes. This will be confirmed in the design space of the reaction and crystallization. In addition, the multivariate experiments mimicked the "worst case" scenario of the proposed commercial equipment and its limitations (example; the heating and cooling profile was executed over hours with the same ability as the manufacturing facility).

section.title: Coating Premix Red KIRSCH2358 Testing Monograph

text.div:
1 Declaration

Red KIRSCH2358 is a red film-coating for tablets. It is a mixture of Hypromellose (USP/NF, Ph. Eur., JP), Macrogol 6000 (USP/NF, Ph. Eur., JP), Titanium Oxide (USP/NF, Ph. Eur., JP), Red ferric oxide (USP/NF, JP).

Properties: Red powder

2 Pharmacopoeia status

As mentioned above, the raw materials used in Red KIRSCH2358 are tested and certified according to the current pharmacopoeias.

3 Test specifications

Test CodeTitle of Test, PrincipleRequirements
Description
10001.01Appearance by visual examinationRed powder
Identification
20443.01Identity by IR (ATR)Complies with a reference spectrum from an authentic reference substance
25301.01Identity of colourantsComplies favorably to authentic reference substance
24221.01Identity of ironPositive
Tests
Ph. Eur.Total ash47.05 – 56.15%

4 General remarks

EquipmentAfter examining its suitability, other equipment than mentioned in this Testing Monograph may also be used. Volumes and masses may be adapted, provided the resulting concentrations lie within the validated range.
ReagentsReagent grade chemicals are used unless otherwise indicated. Deionized or distilled water should be used unless otherwise indicated.
Authentic reference substanceRed KIRSCH2358

5 Tests

5.1 Appearance by visual examination (10001.01)

PrincipleVisual examination
ProcedureExamine the colour and form of the substance on a white base in daylight. Compare with the authentic substance.
Substance requiredCa. 1 g

5.2 Identity by IR (ATR) (20443.01)

Procedure: Determine as indicated in Ph. Eur. Current edition.

Figure 5-1           Comparison spectrum for Red KIRSCH2358

[IMAGE: Untitled.png]

Reference substance, batch: BML5344

5.3 Identity of colourants (25301.01)

PrincipleThe visual comparison of the colour of a film made from both the test substance and authentic reference substance.
Equipment1.     Device for film production, e.g. Spring Blossom 0.008” (Evergreeny.AG.) 2.     White cardboard, e.g. UGC-2 card, 4” × 5” White Cardboard (Boacaard Corp.) 3.     Propeller-type stirrer or blender
ProcedureDispersion: Add 60 ml of boiling de-ionized water into a blender and, while operating at low speed, slowly add 20 g of test substance. After all test substance is added, increase the speed to high and maintain until the test substance is completely dispersed (about 5 minutes). Transfer the dispersed test substance into an amber container and then place into an ice bath for about 30 minutes. Prepare a dispersion also for the authentic reference substance in the same manner, or a use a previous prepared standard film if less than one year old. Film: Pour about 15 ml of the dispersion onto the dull side of the UGC-2 card and spread evenly with the Spring Blossom applicator. Allow the film to dry at room temperature, protected from light.
Substance required10 – 20 mg
EvaluationCompare the colour of the film against a film of the authentic reference substance. The test substance is deemed acceptable if the colour of the film matches that of the authentic reference substance.
AlternativeThe dispersion may also be prepared with 10 g test substance and 30 ml water, using an “Eppendorf” reaction vessel and a Vortex.

5.4 Identity of iron (24221.01)

PrincipleColour reaction
ProcedureAccording to USP/NF – Monograph “Ferric oxide” Test: Identification Instead of the solution of ferric oxide described in USP/NF, use a solution with the same concentration of Red KIRSCH2358.
Substance required0.5 g

5.5 Total Ash (Ph. Eur.)

ProcedureDetermine as required in Ph. Eur. current edition
Substance required1 g

action.title: Principle
action.description: The visual comparison of the colour of a film made from both the test substance and in-house reference substance.

action.title: Equipment
action.description: 1.     Device for film production 2.     White cardboard 3.     Propeller-type stirrer or blender

action.title: Procedure
action.description: Dispersion: Disperse 20 mg of test substance in 60 ml of de-ionized water. 15 mL of the dispersion are needed to prepare a film on a UGC-2 card.  Prepare a dispersion also for the in-house reference substance in the same manner.

action.title: Evaluation
action.description: Compare the colour of the film against a film of the in-house reference substance. The test substance is deemed acceptable if the colour of the film matches that of the authentic reference substance.

action.title: Alternative
action.description: The dispersion may also be prepared using an “Eppendorf” reaction vessel and a Vortex with 10 mg of test substance.

resource.title: Manufacturing process of Sakuramil drug substance (IROHA-corp.)
resource.description: Four-step synthesis CP-4 -> CP-5 (in situ) -> CP-6 -> CP-7 -> CP-9 (Sakuramil). Typical commercial batch size 350 kg.

action.title: Step 1
action.description: CP-4 is combined with methyl chloroformate, lithium-tert-butoxide, and tetrahydrofuran, then stirred. Layers are settled and separated. Precipitates are filtered, rinsed with tetrahydrofuran and dried to yield CP-5.

action.title: Step 2
action.description: CP-5 is combined with sodium borohydride, magnesium chloride, and methanol, then filtered after the reaction completes. Hydrochloric acid is added to the filtrate, layers are settled and separated. Organic layer is distilled with ethanol, and the mixture is stirred with water. Resulting precipitate is filtered, rinsed and dried to yield CP-6.

valueCodeableConcept.text: CPP #3.1 Water addition in the crystallization (% by weight with respect to ethanol)

action.title: Step 3
action.description: CP-6 is combined with tetrahydrofuran, sodium carbonate, and ethyl chloroformate, then heated to reflux. Upon reaction completion, the mixture is filtered and quenched with sodium hydroxide, n-hexane is added, the layers are separated, and the organic layer is distilled with ethanol and stirred with water (CPP #3.1). After filtering and drying it results in CP-7.

action.title: CPP #3.1 Water addition in the crystallization (% by weight with respect to ethanol)

extension.valueString: 98-105 L; then 20 to 35% w/w of ethanol

valueCodeableConcept.text: CPP #4.1 Water addition in the crystallization (% by weight with respect to ethanol)

action.title: Step 4
action.description: CP-7 and CP-8 are combined in methylene chloride followed by the addition of tetra-n-butylammonium bromide and aqueous sodium hydroxide solution while mixing. Upon reaction completion, methylene chloride and water are added (CPP #4.1); ethanol content is monitored by IPC #1. The mixture is separated, washed, cooled (CPP #4.2, IPC #2) and concentrated with ethanol. After filtering and drying it results in CP-9 (Sakuramil).

action.title: CPP #4.1 Water addition in the crystallization (% by weight with respect to ethanol)

resource.title: Manufacturing process of Sakura Bloom 20 mg film-coated tablets (Aparna Pharmaceutical Manufacturing)
resource.description: Wet (fluid-bed) granulation, blending, compression and film-coating. Commercial batch size 520.00 kg (approx. 2,600,000 tablets). No overages. Critical steps: granulation (step 3) and compression (step 8); granule particle size and uncoated tablet hardness are controlled within a design space to ensure dissolution.

action.title: Step 1 - Pre-blending
action.description: Blend 52.000 kg of cellulose, microcrystalline, 26.000 kg of croscarmellose sodium, 353.600 kg of lactose monohydrate and 52.000 kg of Sakuramil drug substance in a diffusion mixer (bin blender).

action.title: Step 2 - Preparation of granulation liquid
action.description: Dissolve 15.600 kg hydroxypropyl cellulose in purified water using a vessel with stirrer to prepare a granulation liquid free from lumps.

action.title: Step 3 - Granulation
action.description: Load the pre-blended material into a fluid bed granulator and add the granulation liquid to achieve wetting of pre-blended material and formation of granules.

action.title: Step 4 - Drying
action.description: Dry the granules using the dryer integrated within the fluid bed granulator unit until loss on drying of 1 - 2 % is achieved.

action.title: Step 5 - Screening
action.description: Sieve the dried granules using a screening mill.

action.title: Step 6 - Lubricant addition
action.description: Sieve 5.200 kg of magnesium stearate through a screen and add it to the granules.

action.title: Step 7 - Final blending
action.description: Blend the mixture using a diffusion mixer (bin blender) to obtain the final blend.

action.title: Step 8 - Tablet compression
action.description: Compress the final blend using a tablet press to obtain the tablet cores.

action.title: Step 9 - Preparation of the coating suspension
action.description: Prepare a homogeneous suspension of the Basic coating premix, red in purified water.

action.title: Step 10 - Film-coating
action.description: Film-coat the tablet cores using the film-coat suspension in a coating pan to achieve the desired film-coat weight gain, followed by drying.

action.title: Step 11 - Inspection
action.description: Collect 10 tablets to perform the Description test and Identification test (RTRT).

action.title: Step 12 - Primary packaging
action.description: The film-coated tablets are primary packaged (HDPE bottle or PA/AL/PVC blister).

action.title: Step 13 - Secondary packaging
action.description: The primary packaged product is packed in a cardboard-based secondary pack.
